ap_physics_c_mechanics-f01.title: Experiment: rotational inertia coefficient of a rolling object

stimulus.description: A student rolls a uniform object without slipping from rest down a ramp of length d = 1.2 m and measures the acceleration a of its center of mass (from timing) at several ramp angles θ. The rotational inertia of the object is I = c M R², where M is the mass, R is the radius and c is an unknown constant.

data.y_label: Acceleration of the center of mass a (m/s^2)
notes: A student rolls a uniform object without slipping from rest down a ramp of length d = 1.2 m and measures the acceleration a of its center of mass (from timing) at several ramp angles θ. The rotational inertia of the object is I = c M R², where M is the mass, R is the radius and c is an unknown constant.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe an experimental procedure to collect the data for the acceleration as a function of the ramp angle. Include the equipment and the measurements, how the independent variable is changed, and one way to reduce the uncertainty in the acceleration.
parts.model_answer: Set each angle from the ramp height and length with a meterstick, time the descent over the marked distance $d$ with a stopwatch or photogate and compute $a=2d/t^2$; change only the angle with the same object and ramp; reduce the uncertainty by repeating each run and averaging the times.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies how the angle is set and measured and how the acceleration is found (timing the descent over a known distance)
required_elements: a way to measure the angle and a way to find the acceleration
common_errors: omits how the acceleration is found

rubric_rows.criterion: Changes only the angle while using the same object and the same ramp (both conditions are needed)
required_elements: change only the angle with the same object and ramp

rubric_rows.criterion: Reduces the uncertainty in the acceleration by repeating the runs and averaging the times, or by using a longer ramp, or by using a photogate (any one earns the point)
required_elements: repeat and average or longer ramp or photogate (any one earns the point)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: For rolling without slipping, the acceleration is $a=\dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1+c}$. Identify the quantities that should be plotted on the vertical and horizontal axes so that the data produce a straight line whose slope can be used to find $c$.
parts.model_answer: Plot $a$ on the vertical axis against $\sin\theta$ on the horizontal axis; the slope is $g/(1+c)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies $a$ (vertical) versus $\sin\theta$ (horizontal)

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On a blank grid whose scale you choose, plot the data in a form that gives a straight line, and draw a best-fit line. Label the axes with quantities and units and use a scale that fills most of the grid.

rubric_rows.criterion: Axes are labeled with quantities and units (sin theta has no units) and the scale fills most of the grid
common_errors: scale uses less than half the grid

rubric_rows.criterion: Plots the five points $(\sin\theta, a)$ accurately
Draws a straight best-fit line through the trend of the points

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Use the best-fit line to determine the rotational inertia coefficient $c$ of the object. Show your work.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 6.64 m/s^2; accept any value within 5 percent)
common_errors: uses data points rather than points on the line

rubric_rows.criterion: Relates the slope to $c$: slope $=g/(1+c)$ so $c=g/\text{slope}-1$
Obtains $c$ of about 0.48 (accept any value consistent with the student's own slope from D1)
alt_solutions: a value of c consistent with the student's own slope from D1
